preconditions.description: n is the length of the array (1 ≤ n ≤ 2,000,000) and m is the number of coupons (1 ≤ m ≤ 100,000).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= q <= 10**5 and 1 <= w <= 10**5 for q, w in coupons)
preconditions.description: Each coupon (q_i, w_i) has distinct q_i values (1 ≤ q_i, w_i ≤ 100,000).

preconditions.expression: len(set(q for q, w in coupons)) == m
preconditions.description: All q_i values in coupons are distinct.

postconditions.description: The output is the maximum total cost Sereja can pay, computed as the sum of w_i for all q_i present in the optimal beautiful array.

postconditions.expression: max_total_cost == sum(w for q, w in coupons if q in optimal_array)
postconditions.description: The maximum total cost is the sum of w_i for all q_i that appear in the optimal beautiful array of length n.

postconditions.expression: all(beautiful(array) for array in possible_arrays if len(array) == n)
postconditions.description: The optimal array must be beautiful, meaning for every pair of distinct elements x and y in the array, there exists a position j (1 ≤ j < n) such that either (array[j] == x and array[j+1] == y) or (array[j] == y and array[j+1] == x).

postconditions.expression: max_total_cost == max(sum(w for q, w in coupons if q in array) for array in possible_arrays if beautiful(array) and len(array) == n)
postconditions.description: The maximum total cost is the highest possible sum of w_i for any beautiful array of length n.
